What happens to my WordPress.com when I die?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 23 Nov 2026

Short answer: WordPress.com says it helps the family or estate decide what happens to a deceased owner's site. Email passwordhelp@wordpress.com with the owner's name or account email (if known), the site address, a short explanation and what you want: make the site private or transfer it to another owner. To transfer ownership, attach a copy of the death certificate plus a legal document showing your authority to act, or a signed, notarized statement. WordPress.com's page describes no setting to plan this in advance, so leave instructions in your digital estate plan.

Key facts

  • Contact: passwordhelp@wordpress.com
  • Options: make the site private or transfer it to another owner
  • Transfer needs a death certificate plus proof of authority or a notarized statement
  • No advance 'legacy' setting described on WordPress.com's page

How do I prepare my WordPress.com account?

  1. Write down in your digital estate plan each site you run on WordPress.com: its address, the email address on the account, and whether it should be kept, made private, handed to someone or deleted.
  2. After a death, email WordPress.com at passwordhelp@wordpress.com.
  3. Include the site owner's name or the account's email address (if you know it), the site's URL, a brief explanation of the situation, and the action you want: making the site private, or transferring it to another owner.
  4. To transfer ownership to another account, attach a copy of the death certificate and either a legal document showing your authority to act for the deceased, or a signed, notarized statement giving your first and last name, current contact details, email address, relationship to the site owner and the action you're requesting.
  5. Once you have access, WordPress.com suggests options such as publishing a post to update readers, adding an 'in memoriam' page, setting up a donation form, making the site private or deleting it.
  6. Update or cancel any paid subscriptions on the site so billing doesn't continue unnoticed.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • The site owner's name or account email address (if known)
  • The site's URL
  • For an ownership transfer: a copy of the death certificate
  • For an ownership transfer: a legal document showing your authority to act, or a signed, notarized statement with your name, contact details, email, relationship and requested action

How long does it take?

WordPress.com publishes no processing time for deceased-owner requests.

What can't be recovered?

  • Paid plans and add-ons keep renewing until someone updates or cancels the subscriptions
  • Anything deleted: WordPress.com lists deleting the site as one option once you have access, so download what you want to keep first

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my WordPress.com when I die?

WordPress.com says it helps the family or estate decide what happens to a deceased owner's site. Email passwordhelp@wordpress.com with the owner's name or account email (if known), the site address, a short explanation and what you want: make the site private or transfer it to another owner. To transfer ownership, attach a copy of the death certificate plus a legal document showing your authority to act, or a signed, notarized statement. WordPress.com's page describes no setting to plan this in advance, so leave instructions in your digital estate plan.

Who do I contact at WordPress.com when a site owner dies?

Email passwordhelp@wordpress.com. WordPress.com says it helps the family or estate decide what happens to the site, such as making it private or transferring it to another owner.

How do I take over a deceased person's WordPress.com site?

Email passwordhelp@wordpress.com asking to transfer ownership to another account, and attach a copy of the death certificate plus a legal document showing your authority to act, or a signed, notarized statement with your name, contact details, email, relationship to the owner and the action you want.

Can WordPress.com make a deceased person's site private?

Yes. WordPress.com lists making the site private as one of the actions you can ask for when you report a deceased site owner.

What can I do with the site once I have access?

WordPress.com suggests publishing an update post, adding an 'in memoriam' page, setting up a donation form, making the site private or deleting it, and updating or cancelling billing subscriptions.

Do I need a lawyer's document to transfer the site?

Not necessarily. WordPress.com accepts either a legal document stating your authority to act for the deceased, or a signed, notarized statement with the details it lists, alongside a copy of the death certificate.
